div.head: Commentary on α 3
div.p: The materials which compose α 3.A–B and PS 29.13–5 most likely derive from a single, more complete entry of the PS which was later split into separate items owing to partly independent processes of excerption and epitomisation. On other similar cases of ‘multiple’ entries in the epitome of the PS and in the indirect tradition, which result from independent processes of excerption and epitomisation from the PS, see Favi (forthcoming). The presence of α 3.A and PS 29.13–5 in the epitome may be explained postulating that αὐτόκερας and αὐτόκρατον were discussed together by Phrynichus, who presented the former as an Atticism and the latter as a more recent equivalent. Although we lack any direct evidence as to how widespread αὐτόκρατον was, the inference above becomes plausible if one takes on board Phrynichus’ comment that αὐτόκρατον was common παρὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς ‘among the laymen’ in PS 29.13–5 (the comment in Ath. epit. 1.32f–33a that αὐτόκρατος was a variety of Chian wine may well provide further support). The similarity between α 3.A and α 3.B (i, ii) is clear, although each of them contains individual differences. Notice, too, that α 3.A and α 3.B (iii) seemingly shared the corrupt reading αὐτοκέραστον (originally the result of a saut du même au même in αὐτό‹κρατον οἷον εὐ›κέραστον, as suggested by Kaibel, is plausible).
